name: Mercado da Ribeira - Time Out Market
seoTitle: Mercado da Ribeira: The Traditional Market Before 2pm
tagline: The domed 1882 market hall at Cais do Sodré, where fish, produce and flower stalls trade on Monday to Saturday mornings.

description.short: The Mercado da Ribeira is Lisbon's old central market hall at Cais do Sodré, opened in 1882. Half is still a council-run fresh market (Monday to Saturday, 06:00–14:00); the other half has been the Time Out food hall since 2014.
description.full:
The Mercado da Ribeira is one building with two halves. This listing covers the building and its working market; the Time Out food hall in the other half has its own listing, so look there if you want lunch. For a cruise passenger the traditional market is a morning stop: it trades Monday to Saturday from 06:00 to 14:00, is best stocked early, and many fish stalls are packing up well before closing. On Sundays it is closed, although the florists open.

Getting there: walk about 26 minutes west from the terminal along the flat riverside, through Praça do Comércio; the market is the large domed building facing Cais do Sodré station. A taxi takes about 10 minutes. If you are on a short call, aim to be inside before 11:00.

What to look at: the fish counters, the fruit and vegetable stalls and the florists, serving local shoppers who buy by the kilo. This is a place to watch and to buy fruit for the day, not to sit down; for a meal, walk through to the food hall. Look up on your way in: the domed front on Avenida 24 de Julho dates from 1930 and is the building's best-known feature.

Weekend extras: on Saturdays the Sábados da Ribeira crafts, antiques and books market fills the central corridor from 10:00 to 19:00, and on Sunday mornings collectors of stamps, coins and postcards meet from 09:00 to 13:00.

What to skip: do not expect a large or picturesque market. Several stalls stand empty, and the city council was tendering vacant spaces in 2026. If you arrive in the afternoon, the traditional side will be closed; the building is then simply a passage to the food hall, Pink Street or the trains.

Context: the hall was Lisbon's main supply market for most of the 20th century, and the council still runs the traditional side.
description.history: Lisbon's riverside produce market began as the Ribeira Velha, near today's Campo das Cebolas. It moved west to the Ribeira Nova, and the present market on Avenida 24 de Julho opened on 1 January 1882. After a major fire, rebuilding took nearly 30 years; the dome added in 1930 earned the building the nickname 'Mesquita do Nabo' (turnip mosque). For decades the Ribeira was the city's main supply market, with wholesalers and retailers under one roof and trading through the night. It lost the wholesale role in the early 2000s, when the regional wholesale market opened outside the centre. In May 2014 half of the hall was let to Time Out, while the council kept the traditional market.
description.significance: It is one of the few places in central Lisbon where residents still buy fresh fish and produce from stallholders, some of whom traded here when the Ribeira supplied the whole city. The building also shows how Lisbon kept a municipal market alive by letting half of it to a food hall: the council still runs the traditional side, and both halves share the same roof and entrances.

directions.general: Located in the historic Cais do Sodré neighborhood, directly adjacent to Cais do Sodré train and metro station on the Tagus River waterfront
directions.fromCruisePort: About 1.9 km west, 26 minutes on flat ground along the river to Cais do Sodré; the market faces the Cais do Sodré station. Taxi about 8-10 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro Green Line to Cais do Sodré station (2-minute walk). Train from Cascais line to Cais do Sodré. Buses 714, 728, 732, 760. Tram 15E and 18E stop nearby. Ferry terminal adjacent for boats from Cacilhas and south bank
directions.parking: Paid parking at Praça Dom Luís I parking garage. Use Telpark app for pre-booking. Limited street parking available

openingTimes.currentStatus: Traditional market open Monday to Saturday mornings; Time Out food hall open daily

seasonal.notes: Fish, meat, fruit and vegetable stalls. Best stocked early; many fish stalls wind down before closing.
Crafts, antiques and books in the central corridor of the ground floor.

seasonal.days: Sunday to Wednesday; Thursday to Saturday

closedDates: Traditional fish and produce market closed on Sundays

admissionPrices.notes: Free entry to the whole building. You pay stallholders directly, by the kilo or by the item.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Monday to Saturday, 08:00–11:00, while the stalls are fully stocked. Saturday adds the crafts market from 10:00.
busyPeriods: Lunchtime, roughly 12:30–14:30, in the food-hall half of the building
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Come in the morning: the traditional market closes at 14:00 and is closed on Sundays. Carry some cash for small purchases. For lunch, walk through to the Time Out food hall in the same building.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 1.5 hours: 26 minutes' walk each way plus 30–40 minutes in the market
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Flat 26-minute riverside walk from the terminal, or about 10 minutes by taxi. The market floor is level, and the council lists it as accessible for reduced mobility, with toilets.
combinableWith: Praça do Comércio and the Baixa
Train to Belém, or to Alcântara-Mar for LX Factory and Pilar 7
Ferry to Cacilhas from Cais do Sodré
tips: Arrive before 11:00: the traditional market runs 06:00–14:00, Monday to Saturday, and fish stalls thin out well before closing.
The fish and produce market is closed on Sundays; only the florists (10:00–20:00) and the collectors' market (09:00–13:00) operate.
Walk from the ship along the flat river via Praça do Comércio, about 26 minutes; a taxi takes about 10.
On Saturdays the Sábados da Ribeira crafts, antiques and books market fills the central corridor from 10:00 to 19:00.
For a meal, walk through to the Time Out food hall in the same building, which opens at 10:00; eat before about 12:30 to find a seat.
Carry some cash for small purchases at the traditional stalls.
Check your cruise line's rules before buying food to take back on board; many restrict it.
Cais do Sodré station opposite has trains to Belém and Cascais, with Alcântara-Mar the stop for LX Factory and Pilar 7.

highlights: Municipal fresh market of fish, meat, fruit and vegetables, Monday to Saturday 06:00–14:00
Domed front on Avenida 24 de Julho, added in 1930
Sábados da Ribeira crafts, antiques and books market on Saturdays
Collectors' market for stamps, coins and postcards on Sunday mornings
Time Out food hall in the other half of the building
Opposite Cais do Sodré station: metro, trains and ferries
facilities: Time Out food hall and bars (other half of the building)
Car park and children's playground nearby at Jardim Dom Luís

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Ground floor is level, with accessible toilets listed by Lisbon City Council. Aisles between stalls can be narrow and wet near the fish counters.
